preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard labs  |  Medium = targeted test or genetic panel ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = biopsy or advanced testing ($1,500–$10,000+)

questions.question: Are two APOL1 high-risk alleles confirmed on genetic testing? (G1/G1, G1/G2, or G2/G2 genotype — requires African ancestry for meaningful interpretation)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high-risk APOL1 genotype with two alleles confirmed; 10-fold increased CKD risk

questions.question: Is African ancestry (Sub-Saharan, African American, or Afro-Caribbean) documented in demographics or social history?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — African ancestry confirmed; APOL1 high-risk variants found almost exclusively in this population

questions.question: Is there a family history of CKD, ESRD, or early dialysis in first-degree relatives?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — strong familial clustering of CKD documented; suggests genetic etiology

questions.question: Is there young adult onset of CKD (age 20–40 years) with rapid eGFR progression?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — early-onset CKD disproportionate to typical hypertensive nephrosclerosis

questions.question: Is there heavy proteinuria (>1 g/day on 24-hr urine or PCR, often nephrotic range in APOL1 nephropathy)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant proteinuria confirmed; reflects disease activity

questions.question: Is there severe, early-onset hypertension requiring ≥3 antihypertensive agents or documented as difficult-to-control?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — resistant or early-severe hypertension confirmed; disproportionate to age

questions.question: Is eGFR decline >5 mL/min/1.73m²/year confirmed on ≥3 serial measurements?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — rapid CKD progression rate confirmed; hallmark of APOL1 nephropathy vs. typical CKD

questions.question: Is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis — especially collapsing variant — confirmed on kidney biopsy? (collapsing FSGS has the strongest APOL1 association)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — FSGS or collapsing glomerulopathy confirmed on biopsy; APOL1 testing strongly indicated

questions.question: Is diabetic nephropathy excluded? (no diabetes, HbA1c <6.5%, no Kimmelstiel-Wilson changes on biopsy)
Are ANA, ANCA, and anti-GBM negative, excluding autoimmune glomerulonephritis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — autoimmune GN excluded; panel negative

high.label: 🔴  ≥80 High confidence APOL1 nephropathy
high.action: optimize ACE inhibitor/ARB therapy targeting BP <130/80 mmHg and proteinuria <0.5 g/day; refer to APOL1-specific clinical trials (inaxaplin, APOL1 channel blocker, in Phase 3); genetic counseling for family members; SGLT-2 inhibitor for added renoprotection

moderate.label: 🟡  60–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: APOL1 genetic testing indicated if not yet done (requires African ancestry confirmation); kidney biopsy for histologic characterization; initiate RAS blockade and SGLT-2 inhibitor

low.label: 🟢  <60 Low confidence
low.action: APOL1 nephropathy unlikely; evaluate alternative CKD etiologies (diabetic nephropathy, hypertensive nephrosclerosis, other GN); APOL1 testing low-yield without confirmed African ancestry
